notes: §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR7: "The literal in the VALUE clause associated with condition-name-1 is placed in the conditional variable according to the rules of the VALUE clause", and "If more than one literal is specified in the VALUE clause, the conditional variable is set to the value of the first literal that appears in the VALUE clause." BindSetCondition resolves each condition-name to its conditional variable (the reference's subscripts select the occurrence); EmitSet takes the first literal of the VALUE clause (the low end when the first entry is a THRU range) and stores the image DataEmitter.ValueImageOf builds with ValueInitializer.InitializerFrom, the same recipe that renders a data item's own VALUE clause, so SET follows the VALUE rules by construction and no edition arm is involved. Probed at --std 85 against §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1: a nonnumeric literal is left-aligned and space-filled in alphanumeric, alphabetic, alphanumeric edited and numeric edited variables with no editing, a JUSTIFIED RIGHT variable is still left-aligned and a BLANK WHEN ZERO variable keeps "000" ("Initialization is not affected by any BLANK WHEN ZERO or JUSTIFIED clause that may be specified."), numeric literals are aligned on the decimal point with their sign in DISPLAY and COMP variables, SPACES, ZERO, HIGH-VALUES and ALL literal fill the variable, a group variable is filled as one area, and a subscripted condition-name sets its own occurrence. The witness sets a variable whose condition-name lists 5 3 7 and displays 5.

next.reason: 1985: "is placed in the conditional variable according to the rules of the VALUE clause"; 2023: "except that when the conditional variable is an alphanumeric group item... to which a table is subordinate, its length is determined as specified in 13.18.38". Both keep VALUE-clause placement and the first-literal rule. 2023 takes a group variable's length from the OCCURS rules when a table is subordinate, and leaves a zero-length variable unchanged.
